work_packages.description: Cross-DLL FLS cleanup of C++ records on two simultaneous guest workers
work_packages.test_status: Two independent native ARM64 macOS runs at 792edaa8 passed the compiled worker package. Both handles stayed unsignaled before release, and each worker’s return or explicit exit invoked its own callback, destructor and heap release before join. The exact missing consumer import was refused before entry and the complete package passed on fresh replay.
work_packages.limitations: Covers scheduled worker termination with FLS in the explicit package loader. Worker PE static TLS, C++ language thread-local destructors, fiber switching and forced termination are outside this witness.

work_packages.description: Character and string destination widths in narrow CRT scanf
work_packages.test_status: Two independent native ARM64 macOS runs at 47df4ac8 passed all four compiled cases, including non-ASCII wide conversion and short secure wide-buffer refusals. All 17 scanner unit tests passed. The legacy runtime_services scanf selection had seven passes and one failure because it still expects %ls to be refused.
work_packages.limitations: Draft PR awaits coordination for the shared legacy test. Wide destinations cover ASCII input under the supported C-locale behavior. Secure buffer sizes count destination elements, and the compiled refusal covers a destination that lacks room for the wide terminator.

work_packages.description: Isolation between overlapping authored PE sessions on the CPU reference backend
work_packages.test_status: Two independent ARM64 runs at 5f5dc0f8 verified two interleaved authored sessions using the same guest journal path. The peer failed cleanup, the surviving session finished with the expected frame results and virtual clock, and a fresh launch restarted both counters.
work_packages.limitations: Covers the CPU reference authored-session API and one controlled cleanup failure. Native Metal, concurrent host execution and full R7 acceptance remain outside this witness.

work_packages.description: CLI provisioning boundary and explicit package process attach
work_packages.test_status: Two independent ARM64 runs at 84196554 verified that LoadLibraryA and GetModuleHandleA both return null with error 126 for the provisioned DLL. Explicit packaging of the same DLL runs process attach before the export returns 42. Missing the DLL fails before entry, and a fresh explicit package run succeeds.
work_packages.limitations: Covers CLI provisioning and explicit package startup. Successful runtime loading of provisioned DLLs and XTRE acceptance remain open.

work_packages.description: GNU exception-object ownership across a DLL throw and an EXE catch
work_packages.test_status: Two independent ARM64 runs at db157391 passed at -O1 and -O2. The DLL throws a noncopyable object, the EXE catches it by const reference, and the producer-defined destructor runs once after the catch. Omitting the shared unwinder fails before entry and a fresh complete package passes.
work_packages.limitations: The authored images link libstdc++ statically and use Xenora’s synthetic pthread services with the explicitly packaged GNU shared SEH unwinder. A separate fully shared MinGW-w64 GCC 16.2.0 package probe against production code equivalent to a1b69294 refused 35 imports before entry, 30 from the installed libstdc++ DLL and five from the installed pthread DLL.

work_packages.description: GNU nested exceptions and same-object rethrow across two DLLs and an EXE
work_packages.test_status: Two independent ARM64 runs at 7b4c4016 passed at -O1 and -O2. The bridge handles a distinct inner object while the outer handler is active, destroys the inner object, and rethrows the original outer object. The EXE sees the original address and the producer-defined outer destructor runs after the EXE catch. Omission of the shared unwinder fails before entry and a fresh complete package succeeds.
work_packages.limitations: The authored images link libstdc++ statically and use synthetic pthread services with the explicitly packaged GNU shared SEH unwinder. The witness covers one nested typed catch and rethrow on the initial guest thread.

work_packages.description: Hosted C-locale collation index using transformed keys and binary search
work_packages.test_status: Two independent ARM64 runs at 45e39b76 passed at -O1 and -O2 with forward and reverse inputs on fresh guest states. The fixture checks byte collation, transform sizing and bounds, six exact sorted positions and two missing composite keys.
work_packages.limitations: The fixture uses the default C locale, one application comparator and successful allocation. Its short transform checks the returned length and bytes outside the supplied capacity.

work_packages.description: Unicode control classification in the bounded GetStringTypeW table
work_packages.test_status: Both baseline guests exited 12 at horizontal tab. Two independent ARM64 runs at fbdb7da4 passed at -O1 and -O2, covering 65 C0, DELETE and C1 controls, explicit and NUL-terminated counts, output bounds, and the intentional zero for sampled units outside the table.
work_packages.limitations: Scope is the existing partial CT_CTYPE1 binding and Xenora’s bounded table. Microsoft defines the flags and Unicode defines the control ranges. Windows classification was not compared at runtime.

work_packages.description: Wide CRT calendar formatting with UTF-16 literals and capacities
work_packages.test_status: At a1b69294, the paired original MinGW-w64 guests print the expected narrow leap-day report through strftime and exit zero at -O1 and -O2. The wide variants exit 125 before entry on the exact time API-set wcsftime import and emit no guest output.
work_packages.limitations: The wide output and capacity checks cannot run until the import is implemented. Scope needs coordination with #1330 for the shared calendar formatter and #312, #535 or #1311 for the standard registry.

work_packages.description: One-byte ANSI character writes to Win32 console screen cells
work_packages.test_status: On the a1b69294-equivalent baseline both compiled guests exited 14 on wide readback of the ANSI write. Two independent ARM64 runs at 34bded2b passed at -O1 and -O2. They checked one-byte ANSI characters, 16-bit attributes, a wide U+03A9 cell and the clipped caller-buffer edge.
work_packages.limitations: Covers the existing bounded screen-cell model and an ASCII input witness. Code-page conversion and ANSI reads are outside this change.

work_packages.description: Compiler-initialized GNU worker TLS across condition-variable waits
work_packages.test_status: Two independent ARM64 runs at 4396f98e passed at -O1 and -O2 with scheduler quanta 64 and 1024. The initial thread and two overlapping workers had distinct addresses and exactly one initializer each. Worker values survived the rendezvous and timeout, and critical-section reacquisition allowed release. The shared virtual clock reached exactly 50,000 ticks for the two concurrent 5 ms waits.
work_packages.limitations: Covers a dynamically initialized scalar with GCC emulated TLS under the synthetic scheduler. Nonzero templates, retirement and C++ thread-local destructors need separate evidence.

work_packages.description: Compare exact wanted-import bindings across registry snapshots
work_packages.test_status: PR #1423 reports seven CLI tests on Python 3.9.6 and 3.12.16 at 995a0835, plus six comparisons using three ARM64 registry snapshots and two exact wanted lists. A local comparison against the 38-lot candidate finds six binding changes across ten runtime controls and no changes across the 35 exact GNU shared-package gaps. The seven Python tests passed in the integration tree.
work_packages.limitations: Reports binding deltas for a selected import corpus. Package-local providers and guest execution require separate loader evidence.

work_packages.description: Release owned Win64 GUID and BLOB values in PropVariantClear
work_packages.test_status: PR #1434 reports three focused loader tests and the existing string-and-value control at ded5b8f0. The four original AMD64 images cover releases, repeated clear, foreign ownership, unwritable and overlapping descriptors. The original fixture builder reproduced the committed images byte-for-byte in the isolated native ARM64 integration tree.
work_packages.limitations: Covers scalar VT_CLSID and VT_BLOB backed by the COM task heap. Overlap rejection is Xenora policy. Other owned variant forms require separate support.

work_packages.description: Bind the existing C structured exception handler through VCRUNTIME140
work_packages.test_status: PR #1441 reports a same-PE pre-entry refusal on a1b69294 and guest status 0 at 05804b77, plus 175 local C SEH and runtime tests. The compiled C guest checks declined and accepting filters, abnormal finally and continuation order. The original fixture builder reproduced the committed images byte-for-byte in the isolated native ARM64 integration tree.
work_packages.limitations: The exact alias inherits the partial UCRT context handler. Microsoft C++ language handlers and the noexcept C export require separate support.

work_packages.description: Resolve UCRT rand, srand and _time64 imports
work_packages.test_status: PR #1399 reports local ARM64 execution at e3f0ae57 for two original AMD64 images after baseline import refusal. The fixtures exercise exact UCRT and API-set routes, legacy RNG controls, and the eight-byte injected clock result. The original fixture builder reproduced the committed images byte-for-byte in the isolated native ARM64 integration tree.
work_packages.limitations: Evidence covers the scoped synthetic RNG and wall clock behavior of the open candidate.

work_packages.description: Bind explicit null-frame AMD64 setjmp and longjmp through VCRUNTIME140
work_packages.test_status: PR #1413 reports two original guest tests and the legacy C control at c37a3be4. The fixture checks return values 73 and 1, saved register and stack state, and nonzero frame refusals. Baseline refuses the exact imports before entry. The original fixture builder reproduced the committed images byte-for-byte in the isolated native ARM64 integration tree.
work_packages.limitations: The two bindings are partial. SEH-backed frame unwinding, C++ destructors and SEH finally handlers require additional support.

ownership_states.DeepSeek-owned: Implementation lane delegated to the DeepSeek coding agent under the maintainer’s ownership.
ownership_states.Catminou-owned: Transferred C/C++ runtime, CRT, ABI, exception, COM and Windows runtime dependency work.
ownership_states.CPU contributor-owned: CPU implementation owned by an existing CPU contributor.
ownership_states.Graphics contributor-owned: RDNA2, shader or graphics implementation owned by an existing graphics contributor.
ownership_states.Awaiting external dependency: Blocked on another owner, scope approval or missing upstream component.
ownership_states.Ready for integration: Implementation completed or published and awaiting merge, integration or review.
ownership_states.Verified: Independently verified completion; no package is promoted here without independent evidence.

workload_policy: Transferred runtime work remains visible but does not count toward the maintainer’s remaining implementation workload.

runtime_acceptance.goal: Original compiled C application with comprehensive supported CRT coverage
runtime_acceptance.evidence: On c8210aaf, Gate A1 and A2 passed 13 tests covering startup, allocation, strings, arithmetic, files, stdio, errors and exit. Open PR #1330 adds byte-exact narrow time formatting and six documented directives, with two independent native fixture runs. Open PR #1385 verifies that escaped percent signs count toward the narrow and wide CRT output limits, with successful sizing at the limit and refusal one unit above it. Open PR #1391 combines CRT environment variables, file scanning, exact floating arithmetic, leap-day UTC formatting and file output in one original hosted C program. It checks absent initial state, a malformed scan and fresh replay at two compiler optimization levels. Draft PR #1401 independently verifies narrow-input scanf character and string destination widths for ASCII, including secure wide buffers and terminator capacity. One shared legacy test still expects %ls to be unsupported and awaits coordination. Open PR #1432 verifies a hosted C-locale index at two compiler optimization levels. It checks exact transform capacity and byte ordering, sorts transformed keys with an ordinal tie-break, and repeats successful and missing binary searches from a fresh state with reversed input.
runtime_acceptance.remaining: Integrate the hosted workloads, consolidate positive and negative coverage by supported CRT family, and record full R1 acceptance. The wide calendar import is awaiting shared file coordination in #1440.

runtime_acceptance.goal: Original compiled C++ application with construction, destruction and STL
runtime_acceptance.evidence: On c8210aaf, the original GNU C++ suite passed three tests. Merged PR #1269 records a separate Microsoft x64 object-lifetime witness. Merged PR #1256 adds a bounded synthetic standard output stream. Open PR #1328 verifies four synthetic codecvt data cells across two independently compiled DLLs with two independent native fixture runs. Open PR #1384 verifies ownership transfer, duplicate-key rejection and exact destruction order in an original hosted GNU std::map guest.
runtime_acceptance.remaining: Microsoft-header stream startup, output, cleanup, failures and independent acceptance.

runtime_acceptance.goal: Multi-DLL application with cross-module runtime ownership
runtime_acceptance.evidence: The package startup suite passed six tests on c8210aaf. PRs #1262 and #1269 record original CRT and C++ ownership witnesses. Merged PR #1280 verifies CRT startup and teardown order across dependent DLLs. Open PR #1328 checks shared runtime data, bidirectional writes and fresh-state zero initialization across the EXE and both DLLs. Open PR #1343 verifies independent static TLS templates and cross-module accesses on the initial guest thread. Draft PR #1360 verifies transactional initial-thread TLS staging and rollback. Open PR #1370 verifies GNU exception propagation through two C DLL frames. Open PR #1387 verifies pre-entry refusal for Microsoft x64 typeid, pointer downcast and side cast, and cast to the complete object through void*. Its RTTI-free control runs virtual calls. Open PR #1398 verifies cleanup across two DLLs: the consumer receives FLS callbacks and the producer destroys and frees each C++ record. Open PR #1418 verifies a noncopyable exception object thrown in the producer DLL, caught by const reference in the EXE and destroyed once by producer-defined code after the catch. Both guests use the same explicitly packaged unwinder. Open PR #1431 adds nested exception ownership across an independent producer DLL, bridge DLL and EXE. The inner object is destroyed in the bridge handler and the EXE catches the original outer object at the same address before the producer-defined destructor runs.
runtime_acceptance.remaining: Independently verify the full ownership milestone. Cover dynamic module lifetime, worker TLS and exception ownership with the fully shared GNU runtime. Microsoft x64 RTTI implementation and cross-module type identity remain open.

runtime_acceptance.goal: Multi-threaded C++ synchronization and thread-local storage
runtime_acceptance.evidence: On c8210aaf, the original C++ worker and four Itanium guard regressions passed. The compiled retry after a throw is tracked separately. Merged PR #1283 checks compiler-emitted abort after a throw and a successful retry on a different guest thread. Open PR #1343 verifies compiler-emitted Microsoft x64 accesses on the initial thread. The worker implementation needs coordination with the scheduler and thread-table owners. Draft PR #1360 verifies initial-thread package TLS storage rollback and retry. Two compiled GNU emulated TLS probes on a1b69294 reproduced a missing constant template and state reused across distinct guest worker IDs. Open PR #1398 verifies two simultaneously live workers, separate FLS values, and destructor and heap cleanup at worker return and explicit exit. Open PR #1451 verifies GCC-emitted dynamic scalar TLS for the initial thread and two overlapping workers. Each worker retains its separate address and value through condition-variable wake and timeout, reacquires the critical section before release, and contributes to the exact five-millisecond synthetic-clock result.
runtime_acceptance.remaining: Cover blocking guard contention, worker PE static TLS, nonzero GNU emulated TLS templates, storage retirement and C++ language thread-local destructors. Coordinate the remaining worker storage work with the C++ and scheduler owners.

runtime_acceptance.evidence: On c8210aaf, two compiled GNU C++ unwinding tests and twelve compiled C structured exception tests passed. Open PR #1345 verifies the documented RaiseException null argument-array rule using original compiled C filters. Open PR #1370 adds a typed GNU catch and destructor order after unwinding through two independently compiled C DLL frames. The throw, catch and destructors reside in the executable. Open PR #1418 records independent ARM64 runs at two optimization levels for a DLL throw, an EXE catch by const reference and the exact order of both stack guards and the producer-defined exception-object destructor. The same package refuses startup without the installed GNU shared SEH unwinder and succeeds again on fresh replay. Open PR #1431 verifies that a bare rethrow after a nested typed catch preserves the outer exception object and the exact guard and destructor order. Two independent ARM64 runs cover both optimization levels, pre-entry refusal without the shared unwinder and fresh replay. Open PR #1441 reports local execution through the exact VCRUNTIME140 C structured exception handler alias with declined and accepting filters, abnormal finally and continuation.
runtime_acceptance.remaining: Cover the Microsoft C++ personality, shared C++ and pthread runtime loading, nested exceptions, unsupported records and post-abort cleanup. A separate fully shared GNU package from the installed MinGW-w64 GCC 16.2.0 toolchain failed before entry with 35 unresolved imports.

runtime_acceptance.goal: Original COM application with supported object lifecycle
runtime_acceptance.evidence: Merged PR #1261 adds opt-in server locks and unload eligibility. Open PRs #1296 and #1324 cover cross-module ownership and simultaneous STA and MTA initialization and lifetime. Open PR #1374 combines same-apartment DLL ownership, a separate worker apartment and balanced factory locking in one original package, including isolated live-object and lock controls. Two independent ARM64 runs passed the fifteen COM and package tests on the combined source tree. Open PR #1434 reports local cleanup of task-owned GUID and BLOB variants, with preserved allocations on the invalid descriptor and ownership controls.
runtime_acceptance.remaining: Integrate the open COM fixtures and record upstream acceptance of the opt-in synthetic lifecycle.

runtime_acceptance.goal: Repeated runtime sessions with resource and state isolation
runtime_acceptance.evidence: The authored-package session harness checks repeated runs and handle cleanup. Merged PR #1262 records a CRT success, failure and fresh-run sequence. Open PRs #1324 and #1328 verify fresh state after exact startup refusal in two additional contracts. Open PR #1344 checks last-event retirement after deliberate failure, exact detach and fresh-success replay. Draft PR #1360 verifies allocation rollback and slot reuse after failed initial-thread TLS staging. Open PR #1370 repeats a successful package run after an exact missing-provider refusal. Open PR #1398 verifies both normal and explicit worker teardown, a missing-consumer refusal, and fresh successful package replay. Open PR #1414 verifies two interleaved CPU reference authored sessions using the same guest journal path. A peer cleanup failure leaves the surviving session’s frame output and virtual clock intact, and a fresh launch resets both counters.
runtime_acceptance.remaining: Exercise callback, worker TLS and shutdown interactions across repeated sessions and obtain independent acceptance.

runtime_acceptance.goal: Runtime performance baseline and measured bottleneck improvements
runtime_acceptance.evidence: PR #1272 records a correctness-gated native qsort improvement for ordered wide records. Draft PR #1360 removes the whole-address-space copy from initial package TLS preparation. Its tests cover rollback and provide correctness evidence. An isolated native release probe of prepare_module_tls with 96 MiB of guest payload already resident reduced median peak resident memory by about 96 MiB. Only module_tls.rs differed, and the control without TLS remained about 98 MiB. Two independent ARM64 reviewers reproduced all four 96 MiB observations exactly.
runtime_acceptance.remaining: Repeat qsort on an idle host with independent measurements, obtain upstream review for the isolated TLS memory result, and measure wall-clock performance on a representative compiled workload.

runtime_acceptance.goal: Runtime integration readiness for the Xenora Title Runtime Environment
runtime_acceptance.evidence: The runtime handoff and persistent authored-session API are merged. Runtime and XTRE retain their respective ownership. Open PR #1344 supplies another explicit-package teardown witness for the existing runtime API. Draft PR #1360 and open PR #1370 add explicit-package TLS rollback and GNU unwind evidence for the current runtime boundary. Open PR #1416 verifies that CLI provisioning leaves the DLL unavailable to LoadLibraryA and GetModuleHandleA. Explicit packaging of the same provider executes process attach before the export returns 42. The dynamic-loading handoff is recorded in issue #923.
runtime_acceptance.remaining: Complete the dynamic-loading handoff, agree the startup, unwind, ownership and shutdown interfaces with the XTRE owner, and run integrated acceptance.
